newsitem.title: UK: Glaxo gets German approval for Raxar.
newsitem.headline: Glaxo gets German approval for Raxar.

text.p: British drugs and pharmaceuticals group Glaxo Wellcome Plc announced on Friday it had received approval from German regulatory authorities to market Raxar (grepafloaxin), an antibiotic to treat respiratory tract infections.
Glaxo said Germany would act as the reference state for approvals throughout the European Union.
Raxar is a fluoroquinolone, antibiotic which Glaxo Wellcome said was able to overcome some of the resistance to existing antibiotics. The drug will be marketed in Germany as Vaxar.
The drug has been approved for treatment of contagious pneumonia, acute bacterial exacerbation of chronic bronchitis and a number of sexually transmitted diseases.
Last month analysts at Credit Suisse First Boston said Raxar could have peak sales of $500 million a year.
Raxar was licensed from Otsuka Pharmaceutical Co Ltd of Japan.
The German approval of Raxar follows news on Thursday that Glaxo Wellcome had won approval in Britain to market a new diabetes drug, Romozin, under license from Japan's Sankyo Co .
